intro:
Use it for the small readings and controls that sit around a piece of work rather than in a form: a count with its trend, a percentage, a timecode with play and skip, a speed, which section is showing, how far an export has got. Every pill has the same height and surface, so a row of them reads as one strip of instruments.

A pill is built from parts written in the order they read. Each pill in the board above has its own example further down this page. At an end that is a round button, a segmented choice or a ring, the pill pulls its padding in so the circle sits concentric with it.

For a single figure with a label and a badge, use [Stat](/docs/web/components/stat). For a status word, use [Badge](/docs/web/components/badge).
usage:
<Micro>
  <Micro.Text value="12.4k" label="listens · 30 days" />
  <Micro.Spark values={[4, 5, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11]} tone="info" />
  <Micro.Delta value={9} />
</Micro>

parts.Text: A value over a muted line saying what it is.
parts.Label: One muted word or phrase on a single line, such as "Speed".
parts.Mono: A reading in mono figures, for times and counts that change in place. `muted` dims it, for the second half of a pair.
parts.Spark: A run of thin bars, oldest first. The newest is drawn in `tone`. They rise when first shown.
parts.Ring: A ring that sweeps to `value`, from 0 to 100. It is a meter, named by `label`.
parts.Delta: A change with its sign and an arrow, green when up and red when down. `inverted` swaps them, for a reading where lower is better.
parts.Pulse: A heartbeat line that beats while `live`, for a reading taken continuously.
parts.Button: A round button. `ghost` shows its circle only when pointed at, and `aria-pressed` fills it.
parts.Separator: A short upright rule between two groups.
parts.Segments: A choice of a few, with a marker that slides to the chosen one. The arrow keys move it.
parts.Stepper: A number between a minus and a plus, with `min`, `max` and `step`. Its digits roll as it changes, and the arrow keys move it.
parts.Progress: A label and a count over a row of ticks that fill as the work is done: one tick each, up to 16.
parts.Switch: A switch sized for the pill. Put a `Micro.Text` before it for what it turns on.
parts.Faces: Overlapping faces, with initials where there is no picture. Four show and the rest are counted.
parts.Input: A bare field that takes the pill's remaining width.
parts.Kbd: A key or a chord in a cap.

examples.title: A count and its trend
examples.description: `Micro.Text` gives the value and what it counts. `Micro.Spark` draws its recent values as bars, oldest first, with the newest in `tone`. `Micro.Delta` says how much it moved.

examples.title: A percentage
examples.description: `Micro.Ring` sweeps to `value`, from 0 to 100. At the pill's start it is pulled in to sit concentric with the end. Give it a `label`, since it is read as a meter.

examples.title: Playback
examples.description: A solid `Micro.Button` for the main action and `variant="ghost"` buttons for the rest. `Micro.Separator` sets the time apart, and `Micro.Mono` keeps its figures from shifting as they change. `muted` dims the total.

examples.title: A choice of a few
examples.description: `Micro.Segments` holds `Micro.Segment`s, with a marker that slides to the chosen one. The arrow keys move it. A ghost button after it adds to the choices.

examples.title: A number between bounds
examples.description: `Micro.Stepper` sits between a minus and a plus, with `min`, `max` and `step`. Its digits roll as it changes, and the arrow keys, Home and End move it once it has focus. `format` and `suffix` set how it is written.

examples.title: A pair of actions
examples.description: Ghost buttons on their own make a pill of icon actions. `aria-pressed` fills a button that stays on, such as a bookmark.

examples.title: A live reading
examples.description: `Micro.Pulse` beats beside a reading taken continuously, in `tone`. `Micro.Delta` with `inverted` draws a rise in red, for a reading where lower is better.

examples.title: Progress
examples.description: `Micro.Progress` puts a label and a count over a row of ticks, one per unit up to 16, that fill as work is done. The tick being worked on is drawn a little longer. A button at the end pauses it.

examples.title: Who approved
examples.description: `Micro.Faces` overlaps up to four faces, with initials where there is no picture, and counts the rest. A `Micro.Label` and a glyph say what they did.

examples.title: A search
examples.description: `Micro.Input` takes the pill's remaining width. Give the pill a width. `Micro.Kbd` shows the key that focuses it.

examples.title: A setting
examples.description: `Micro.Switch` is a switch sized for the pill. Put a `Micro.Text` before it saying what it turns on and where.

examples.title: A balance
examples.description: A glyph, a `Micro.Mono` figure and a `Micro.Label` for its unit.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `size="sm"` is 40px tall and `md`, the default, is 48px. The parts inside follow the pill's size.

notes:
### Tones

Bars, rings, ticks and the pulse are drawn in the text's colour unless `tone` names a theme colour: `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive`. Use a tone for what a reading means, not to decorate it.

### Motion

The spark's bars rise once when they first show, the ring sweeps whenever its value changes, the stepper's digits roll, the segment marker slides, and ticks fill as progress is made. With reduced motion each change happens at once and the pulse stops.

### Screen readers

`Micro.Ring` is a meter and `Micro.Progress` a progress bar, both read with their values. `Micro.Segments` is a radio group and `Micro.Stepper` a spin button. A `Micro.Button` that holds only a glyph needs an `aria-label`, as does `Micro.Input`.
